app_summary: An online shop selling astronomy products, based on the OpenTelemetry Demo. It is built with polyglot microservices (Go, Java, .NET, Python, Node.js, Rust, ...) communicating via gRPC and HTTP behind an Envoy frontend-proxy, with Kafka for asynchronous order processing and Valkey as cart store. Supported Operations: View product catalog, Receive product recommendations and ads, Add item to cart, Checkout with selected items, Currency conversion, Process payment, Generate shipping quotes, Send order confirmation emails

The DNS server used for the lookup is the cluster DNS at 10.96.0.10; the message "server misbehaving" indicates the DNS lookup failed with a server-side DNS error (e.g., SERVFAIL) rather than a simple NXDOMAIN, though the immediate trigger is the invalid hostname lookup
Other downstream services in the traces (cart, product-catalog, currency, shipping, quote) appear to succeed — the failure is localized to the payment resolution and charge step

Confirmed hypothesis: the errors are DNS resolution failures for the payment hostname; root cause diagnosed as checkout failing to resolve 'badAddress' via cluster DNS, causing PaymentService/Charge to return UNAVAILABLE and the checkout flow to error

Actionable remediation implied: fix the payment hostname configuration in checkout (replace 'badAddress' with the correct service hostname) or fix the cluster DNS (10.96.0.10) if it is returning SERVFAIL for valid names

final_report.root_cause: The checkout service attempted to resolve and contact an invalid payment hostname "badAddress" at runtime. DNS lookups for "badAddress" against the cluster DNS (10.96.0.10) failed with "server misbehaving" (SERVFAIL), causing the gRPC PaymentService/Charge RPCs to return UNAVAILABLE/INTERNAL and the checkout flow to surface 500 errors. In short: an application-level misconfiguration (or incorrect runtime value) in checkout caused it to use the bogus hostname "badAddress", which led directly to DNS resolution failures and a failed charge path.
final_report.evidence_summary: 1) ~20 error traces sampled from the frontend-proxy/checkout flow all contain identical error text: "dns: A record lookup error: lookup badAddress on 10.96.0.10:53: server misbehaving" (example traceIDs: 6f809b20..., f14b93..., 681ae4...). 2) Traces show the failing RPC is oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge and that these spans return rpc status UNAVAILABLE with otel.status_description containing the DNS lookup failure. 3) The checkout PlaceOrder span surfaces the payment failure as an INTERNAL error: "failed to charge card: ... lookup badAddress on 10.96.0.10:53: server misbehaving". 4) Deployment inspection shows checkout Deployment has PAYMENT_ADDR=payment:8080 (priority #2), and the payment Service/Pod are present and healthy (priority #5), which rules out a straightforward service-name/port mismatch — but does not contradict the traces that show the runtime used "badAddress". 5) Cluster DNS (kube-dns) Service and Endpoints exist and point to two ready CoreDNS pods (10.96.0.10 → endpoints 10.244.0.2 & 10.244.0.4) and the CoreDNS pods are Running/Ready with no restarts observed; CoreDNS logs could not be retrieved in the earlier run, so transient resolver-level failures cannot be fully demonstrated, but service/pod health and endpoints indicate the DNS control-plane is present and registered.
final_report.investigation_summary: Priority-driven investigations focused first on trace evidence (priority #1) which clearly showed DNS lookup failures for hostname "badAddress" during PaymentService/Charge calls. Next (priority #2) we validated checkout's declared PAYMENT_ADDR and the payment Service/Pod to rule out an obvious service-name/port mismatch; payment is healthy and payment:8080 is configured as expected. CoreDNS and kube-dns Service/Endpoints were inspected (priorities #3 and #4): CoreDNS pods are Running/Ready with no restarts and kube-dns endpoints point to them (10.96.0.10 → 10.244.0.2 & 10.244.0.4). Checkout and payment pod logs returned no additional clues (no DNS errors logged), so the strongest, most direct evidence remains the distributed traces showing checkout attempted to resolve "badAddress" via cluster DNS and failed. Combining all findings yields the causal chain: checkout used a bogus hostname (badAddress) → DNS query to cluster DNS (10.96.0.10) returned SERVFAIL / "server misbehaving" → gRPC PaymentService/Charge returned UNAVAILABLE → checkout transaction failed and returned INTERNAL/500 to the user.
